name: Research Project Report
description: Structured project/progress report for a research project (master, PhD, funded project). Compiles experiment records, data files, photos and notes into a documented report with full claim-to-source traceability. NOT a thesis writer: it assembles and cites what exists, and flags what is missing. Structure aligned with common institutional progress-report and lab-report conventions.

sections.title: Objective & Research Question
sections.notes: The objective must come from the sources (proposal, notes, supervisor email). If none found: [MISSING: research_question] — the engine never invents a research aim.

sections.title: Method & Experimental Setup
sections.notes: Reproducibility rule: a competent peer should be able to repeat the setup from this section. Photos of the rig are mapped here. Every parameter cites a source (notebook entry, config screenshot, instrument photo).

sections.title: Data Collected

required_facts.label: At least one recorded measurement / dataset

sections.notes: STRICT section: every value cites a fact from a data file, instrument photo, or notebook. CSVs indexed by MarkItDown provide the fact source. Summary statistics only if present in sources — the engine does not compute statistics in v1.

sections.title: Results & Observations
sections.notes: Content rule 'separate_observation_from_interpretation': the generated text states what the sources show, attributed per claim. Interpretation beyond the sources is not generated — that is the researcher's job, and the section ends with an editable block reserved for it.

sections.title: Deviations & Issues
sections.notes: Failed runs, equipment issues, protocol changes — pulled from notes and photos tagged damage/deviation. Honest reporting section; funders and supervisors value it.

sections.title: Status & Next Steps

required_facts.label: At least one stated next step

sections.notes: Next steps come from the researcher's own notes in the sources. If none exist: [MISSING: next_step] — the plan is the researcher's, not the engine's.

sections.title: Source Register
sections.notes: Auto-generated from the project index: every file with its caption and which sections cite it. This is the traceability appendix — for a student, the audit trail that the report reflects real project material; assembled by code, zero AI tokens.

sections.title: Declaration
sections.boilerplate: This report was compiled from the project source material listed in the Source Register. All factual claims are traceable to the cited sources. Interpretations and conclusions are the author's own.
sections.boilerplate_no: Denne rapporten er sammenstilt fra prosjektets kildemateriale slik det fremgår av kilderegisteret. Alle faktapåstander er sporbare til de siterte kildene. Tolkninger og konklusjoner er forfatterens egne.
sections.notes: The declaration makes the tool's role explicit — assembly and citation, not authorship of ideas. This is the academic-integrity posture, stated in the document itself.
